case_name: Manoranjan Prasad Mandal vs Moni Mandal
facts_of_case: Appeal against a decree/judgment passed by the Family Judge. Delay of 27 days pointed out by the Office regarding the issue of limitation.

legal_principles.principle: The period of limitation for filing an appeal from a decree or order made by the Court in any proceedings shall be ninety days.
legal_principles.held: Thus, it is evident from Section 28 of the Act of 1955 provides for appeals from decrees and orders. Prior to Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 2003, section 28(4) provided a period of 30 days only for filing an appeal.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Section X
cited_cases: Savitri Pandey v. Prem Chandra Pandey (supra)

legal_principles.principle: Family Courts should adopt an approach radically different from that adopted in ordinary civil proceedings and make reasonable efforts at settlement before the commencement of the trial.
legal_principles.held: The Law Commission in its 59th report (1974) had also stressed that in dealing with disputes concerning the family the court ought to adopt an approach radically different from that adopted in ordinary civil proceedings and that it should make reasonable efforts at settlement before the commencement of the trial.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is within the period of limitation as per the judgment dated 16.12.2020 passed by the Co-ordinate Division Bench of this Court.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act implications
preparing appeals against Family Court judgments
